title: Fivetran Monthly Active Rows Cost Spike
dataSources: Fivetran REST API connector status (`fivetran:connector`), log-service sync events (`fivetran:log`), and usage/MAR exports.
app: Fivetran REST API (`/v1/connectors`, `/v1/metadata`) and Fivetran Platform Connector logs via HEC scripted inputs; Fivetran log-service events (`fivetran:log`).
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=fivetran:log event="records_modified"
| timechart span=1d sum(count) as mar by connector_id
| untable _time connector_id mar
| eventstats avg(mar) as avg_mar, stdev(mar) as sd_mar by connector_id
| where mar>avg_mar+3*sd_mar
| sort - mar
description: Tracks Fivetran monthly-active-rows (MAR) per connector and flags days where a connector's row volume spikes far above its own baseline, the primary driver of Fivetran cost.
value: Fivetran bills on MAR; an unexpected spike (a bad re-sync or an upstream backfill) can blow the monthly budget, and per-connector anomaly detection catches it within a day.
implementation: Ingest Fivetran log-service records_modified events; schedule daily and alert on 3-sigma MAR spikes for any connector.
visualization: Timechart of MAR per connector, anomaly table, cost projection.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how many rows each data connector moves so a surprise spike that would inflate the bill is caught the same day.
